title: Report dispatch design
description: Reports need to plug into Run without Run depending on them. Options: a registry each report story fills, or Run importing all six reports. Registry keeps filter and report stories ordered correctly (filters and CLI before reports).

options.label: Registry populated by each report story
Run imports all report writers directly

title: Usage error output
description: Sources fix exit code 2 and empty stdout but not the stderr text. Choosing a one-line usage summary on stderr.

title: Blank line definition and line length
description: A blank line is one empty after trimming whitespace. The reader uses bufio.Reader rather than Scanner so long lines are not rejected by a token limit.

title: --since later than --until
description: Sources do not say. Choosing the narrowest reading: empty result, exit 0, not a usage error.

title: Register behavior on duplicate report name
description: Register overwrites any writer already registered under the same name, without panicking. Duplicate registration is silent. Is that acceptable, or should it fail loudly on replan?
system_choice: Register overwrites any writer already registered under the same name, without panicking. Duplicate registration is silent. Is that acceptable, or should it fail loudly on replan?

title: Wrong-typed returncode, timed_out and token values
description: A non-integer returncode is treated as nil, a non-boolean timed_out as false, and a non-integer token or elapsed value as zero. A float such as 12.0 in a token field counts as zero. The spec only named absent, null and non-numeric values, so I took the strictest reading. Is that acceptable?

title: Structured skip record
description: Warnings were required on the warning writer only. I also added Result.Skips, a slice of {Line, Reason}, so the warning line-number test can read the line back as a value instead of matching text. Skipped is still the count. Is this acceptable, or should it move out of Result on replan?

title: Writer registration and test isolation
description: Report writers register from an init() in internal/report, with an exported report.Register() that re-registers all six. cmd/ddkstat imports the package for its side effect. The new internal/cli tests call report.Register() because existing tests overwrite registry entries globally. I removed TestRunUnregisteredReportExit0WritesNothing, since every known report now has a writer. Is that acceptable, or should registration move on replan?
